# markdown-regex API

Package: `markdown-regex` (same name on GitHub and npm).
Node 20+. Named exports only. Flags: `g` on every regex; `m` when `^`/`$` need line anchors. Reset `.lastIndex` between `.test()` calls.

GitHub 2.1.0. npm `latest` may still be 1.2.0.

## extract(markdown: string): ExtractResult

Runs fenced code, then inline code (both removed from the working string), then the remaining patterns. Use this instead of applying `REGEXP_LINK` / `REGEXP_STRONG` to raw Markdown if you care about false matches inside code.

```ts
interface ExtractResult {
  headers: { level: number; text: string }[];
  links: { text: string; url: string }[];
  images: { alt: string; url: string }[];
  bold: string[];
  italic: string[];
  strikethrough: string[];
  blockquotes: string[];
  horizontalRules: string[];
  unorderedLists: string[];
  orderedLists: string[];
  codeBlocks: { language: string; code: string }[];
  inlineCode: string[];
  html: string[];
}
```

## Regex exports

| Export | Match | Non-match | Flags |
|---|---|---|---|
| REGEXP_HEADER | `# Title` | `Title\n=====` (setext) | gm |
| REGEXP_H2 | `## Title` | `# Title` | gim |
| REGEXP_H3 | `### Title` | `## Title` | gim |
| REGEXP_IMAGE | `![alt](url)` | `[alt](url)` | g |
| REGEXP_LINK | `[text](url)` | `[text][id]` (reference) | g |
| REGEXP_STRONG | `**bold**`, `__bold__` | `*not bold*` | g |
| REGEXP_ITALIC | ` *italic* ` | `not*italic*` | g |
| REGEXP_DEL | `~~gone~~` | `~gone~` | g |
| REGEXP_CODE | `` `code` `` | fenced blocks | g |
| REGEXP_INLINE_CODE | `` `code` `` | escaped backticks | g |
| REGEXP_FENCED_CODE | fenced ``` or ~~~ blocks | indented-only code | g |
| REGEXP_HTML | `<div>`, `</span>`, `<br/>` | `<<not-a-tag>>` | gi |
| REGEXP_Q | `:"quoted":` | `"quoted"` | g |
| REGEXP_BLOCKQUOTE | `\n> quote` | start-of-string `>` without a leading newline | g |
| REGEXP_HR | `\n-----` (5+ dashes) | `---` | g |
| REGEXP_PARAGRAPH | text between newlines | heuristic only | g |
| REGEXP_BR | two or more newlines | a single `\n` | g |
| REGEXP_EMPTY_BLOCKQUOTE | `</blockquote><blockquote>` | a real blockquote | g |
| REGEXP_UL_LIST | `* item` at line start | `- item` | gm |
| REGEXP_OL_LIST | `1. item` at line start | `1) item` | gm |
| REGEXP_EMPTY_UL | `</ul><ul>` | a real list | g |
| REGEXP_EMPTY_OL | `</ol><ol>` | a real list | g |

## Subpath exports

All subpaths are bundled into the single `markdown-regex` package (no extra installs, zero runtime deps).

### `markdown-regex/frontmatter`

```ts
import { parseFrontmatter } from 'markdown-regex/frontmatter';

parseFrontmatter('---\ntitle: Hi\ntags: [a, b]\n---\n# Body');
// { data: { title: 'Hi', tags: ['a', 'b'] }, content: '# Body', hasFrontmatter: true }
```

| Export | Kind | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| parseFrontmatter(markdown) | function | Returns `FrontmatterResult`: `data` (object or `null`), `content` (body without the fence), `hasFrontmatter` |
| FrontmatterResult | type | |

Supported YAML subset: `key: value` scalars (string, number, boolean, null), nested maps by 2-space indent, inline lists `[a, b]`, block lists `- item`. Not supported: anchors, tags, `|` / `>` multiline literals. On a YAML parse error `data` is `{}` and `hasFrontmatter` stays `true`.

### `markdown-regex/blocks`

```ts
import { extractCustomBlocks, registerBlockRule } from 'markdown-regex/blocks';

registerBlockRule({ name: 'warning', order: 1 });
extractCustomBlocks(':::note\nhi\n:::\n\n:::warning\ncareful\n:::');
// [{ name: 'warning', body: 'careful', raw: ':::warning…', index: … }, { name: 'note', … }]
```

| Export | Kind | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| extractCustomBlocks(markdown) | function | Flat `:::name … :::` blocks → `CustomBlock[]` (`name`, `body`, `raw`, `index`). `:::` inside fenced code is ignored |
| REGEXP_CUSTOM_BLOCK | RegExp | The flat block pattern (global) |
| registerBlockRule({ name, order? }) | function | Optional ordering registry; lower `order` first (default 100) |
| listBlockRules() / clearBlockRules() | function | Inspect / reset the registry (module-level state, reset it in tests) |
| CustomBlock, BlockRule | type | |

Nested `:::` containers are out of scope (issue #407).

### `markdown-regex/email`

| Export | Kind | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| prepareForEmail(markdown) | function | Placeholder: returns the input unchanged today. Do not rely on it to transform anything yet |
| EMAIL_PACKAGE_VERSION | string | Internal marker |

### `markdown-regex/cleanup`

| Export | Kind | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| REGEXP_EMPTY_UL / REGEXP_EMPTY_OL / REGEXP_EMPTY_BLOCKQUOTE | RegExp | Run on **HTML** after Markdown→HTML to merge adjacent empty containers |

## CLI

```bash
npx markdown-regex links README.md     # [{ "text": "…", "url": "…" }]
npx markdown-regex headers doc.md      # [{ "level": 1, "text": "…" }]
npx markdown-regex images doc.md       # [{ "alt": "…", "url": "…" }]
npx markdown-regex extract doc.md      # full ExtractResult
cat doc.md | npx markdown-regex links  # stdin (or pass `-`)
```

Pretty-printed JSON on stdout. `-h` / `--help` prints usage.

## Limits

Nested emphasis, setext headers, reference links, and matching inside code (unless you use `extract()`) are out of scope.
